```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r setup}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/scout.db")
postings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "scout_postings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

```{r sql_dplyr}
# Today: dplyr, on the data frame from dbReadTable()
postings |> # pipe = then ; take postings, then
  dplyr::filter(remote == 1) |> # filter by remote jobs, then
  dplyr::count(company, sort = TRUE) |> # count by company
  head(10) 
```

```{r}
# can do variable = jobs |>  and set the variable to the output of the query
jobs = postings |>
  dplyr::select(company, title, location_state, remote, category, posted_at, last_seen_at)
jobs

jobs |>
  dplyr::select(company, location_state, remote, posted_at, last_seen_at) |>
  dplyr::filter(remote == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(days_open = as.numeric(as.Date(last_seen_at) - as.Date(posted_at))) |> # mutate creates new column, which this creates a column that says how many days the posting has been open for
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(days_open)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(company) |>
  dplyr::summarize(n = dplyr::n(), avg_days = mean(days_open))
```



# Answering the question about data types

```{r}
jobs = postings |>
  dplyr::select(company, location_state, remote, posted_at, last_seen_at) |>
  dplyr::filter(remote == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    posted_at = as.Date(posted_at), # force change the column into date format
    last_seen_at = as.Date(last_seen_at),
    days_open = as.numeric(last_seen_at - posted_at)
    ) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(days_open)) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(company) |>
  dplyr::summarize(n = dplyr::n(), avg_days = mean(days_open))
```

```{r helpers}
jobs = jobs |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_at"), as.Date))    # both dates at once
jobs |> dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), mean))
```


## Demo

```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/scout.db")
postings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "scout_postings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

jobs = postings |>
  dplyr::select(company, title, location_state, remote, category, posted_at, last_seen_at) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_at"), as.Date),
                days_open = as.numeric(last_seen_at - posted_at))
```

```{r q1_by_category}
# which category is remote friendly
# to answer that, the logic would be as follows:
# - find number of jobs per category
# - normalize the number of remote jobs per category by dividing by the total jobs

jobs |> 
  # I want to move from unit of analysis being a job posting to a category
  dplyr::group_by(category) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings= dplyr::n(),
    remote_share = mean(remote)
  ) 
```
